The email agentic cell: why connecting Gmail to agents the usual way is a security mess, and the architecture we will build instead, with one gateway agent that alone touches Gmail, a digital twin of the mailbox in a vault that people and agents work on together, signed proposals, approvals and even reads on append lanes, and behaviour policies at five altitudes

Deploy sgit in your own environment, from a CI pipeline: one Docker image, ciphertext in your own S3 bucket in the region you choose, an access token only you hold, and the pipeline pattern we learned building the AgentiCCells site factory, a protected environment, AWS through OpenID Connect with no keys, a role that trusts one repository and one environment, check workflows before anything real, and a full cycle that deploys, tests and tears down

Your own agentic cell, end to end: how a person asks for a site like the ones we made for Yiheng Wang and Silvio Switha, through a key pair in the browser, a vault they fill themselves and the site factory, with only three human gates, and then continues in their own Claude on their own repository

Your website, from a vault: how to show someone five versions of their own website without publishing anything, sealed in an encrypted sgit vault and opened with a QR code, a link or a zip on one drop page, the demo pipeline from a name to an email, and how a demo becomes their sovereign website without starting again
sgit in GitHub Actions, side by side: a showcase repository and site that runs four ways of moving a vault between jobs on every run, measured, with a budget for its LLM steps
Inside the no-server studio: an infographic studio built to the no-server blueprint, what is real, what is simulated, and the business plan in its vault

Inside Kitewing Websites: a made-up studio that sells websites you own, and three made-up client sites built as vault apps, a potter's catalogue, a community garden and a local plumber's guides library, each one file, each different, and each ready to be changed by talking to it

Our workflow on Odoo 20, built and measured: a bills agent with no Odoo credential, a policy check that allowed two proposals and stopped three, a signed approval, a narrow broker, a grant measured from Odoo itself by a new module, and what Odoo's default user role quietly allows

HeritageTech, together: how our open-source stack could plug into UAlgTec Heritage, the University of the Algarve's new European centre of excellence for heritage science and technology, mapped from the dig to the museum, with encrypted evidence vaults per site, signed finds, graphs of every excavation, agents with written policies, and what I would write in its "start a conversation" form
Cedar and the policy vault: a debrief on the policy language agents are adopting, where our behaviour policies and sgit vaults meet it, and a brief for the MVP
secrets.sgit.ai on public keys: no more shared keys, eight ways a secret moves, a vault for the private key, and the commercial service it becomes
Inside the Pellbridge agents: six behaviour policies with the FCA's four elements filled in, one day of their work replayed through the gate, and the files that make it
Knowledge graphs in the era of LLMs: what the KGELL COST Action is doing, and what 309 graphs built by agents in a working newsroom can bring to its working group on construction
The legal AI services map: 44 companies scored on who does the work, who stands behind it, and whether an agent can hire them, with the evidence in a public vault
